## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One critical defect needs fixing: `save_report` ignores write failures, still prints that the report was saved, and returns 0, so users are told a save worked when it didn't. This review read all of `app/reports.py` and `tests/test_reports.py` and traced each new function against its tests; no tests were run. `cleanup_report` catches only `FileNotFoundError`, explains why in a comment, and has a test (`test_cleanup_preserves_other_errors`) checking that other `OSError`s still reach the caller.

## Changes
Adds `save_report`, which writes the rendered report to a path and prints where it went, and `cleanup_report`, which deletes a temporary report and treats a missing file as already cleaned up. Also adds tests for both functions.

## Critical
- app/reports.py:8 — silent-failure — Propagate write errors instead of reporting success — When `path.write_text` raises `OSError` (for example, the destination's parent directory doesn't exist, as in `tmp_path / "missing" / "report.txt"`), `except OSError: pass` discards it, then line 10 prints `Report saved to {path}` and line 11 returns 0. Nothing is logged, and the return value is the same as on success, so the caller can't tell the save failed. — Users and scripts that check the exit code are told the report was saved when no file exists, and the report is lost without any error to act on. — Fix: Remove the `try`/`except` or re-raise, and print the success message only after `write_text` returns. Also update `test_save_with_unavailable_destination` (tests/test_reports.py:13), which has no assertions and passes while the bug is present, to expect the error, e.g. `with pytest.raises(OSError):`, or a non-zero return with no success message.
